rounds.text: Modis Navnirman Ltd is significantly under-appreciated by the market, trading at a P/E of just 24.7x [E1] while delivering explosive top-line and bottom-line expansion, including compounded sales growth of 70% over 5 years [E14] and a 138% CAGR in profit over the same period [E17]. The company's underlying fundamentals vastly outperform sector benchmarks, boasting an ROE of 20.61% against a sector median of 4.55% [E9], and an ROCE of 23.19% compared to the sector's 5.21% [E10]. This exceptional operating performance is further validated by a rules-based screen score of 99 out of 100 with high confidence [E56] and a discounted cash flow model indicating an intrinsic value of Rs 748 per share, which leaves a substantial margin of safety of 38.9% [E41]. Institutional confidence is swelling, demonstrated by foreign institutions increasing their stake to 12.27% from 0.00% in Sep 2023 [E37] and overall institutional money flow reading positive [E39]. Conceded: the dividend yield is 0.00% [E4], and operating cash flow was a negative Rs 2 Cr in Mar 2026 [E30]. Nevertheless, management maintains a robust portfolio of 25 premium residential projects across Bombay [E71], expects healthy project margins of 20% to 30% [E67], and forecasts sustained high housing demand driven by a young median age of 29 years [E70].

The bull case points to strong historical growth and profitability metrics, but the underlying cash generation tells a deeply concerning story of cash conversion failure [E29]. Operating cash flow and free cash flow both plunged to negative Rs 2 Cr in March 2026, meaning reported accounting profits are entirely divorced from actual cash landing in the bank [E30, E31]. Conceded: the company boasts a high return on capital employed and stellar sales growth figures [E10, E16]. However, this rapid top-line expansion has coincided with a sharp escalation in borrowings, which quadrupled from Rs 6 Cr to Rs 24 Cr between September 2025 and September 2026 [E34]. Furthermore, the company pays a dividend yield of exactly 0.00% despite its reported earnings, denying cash returns to shareholders while insider alignment quietly weakens [E4, E36]. Promoter holding has dropped by 7.24 percentage points over the last three years down to 63.79%, signaling waning commitment from the insiders who know the business best [E36, E55]. Finally, operational headwinds are emerging as evidenced by the Rashmi Govind Dalvi project being placed on hold due to a government-imposed stay on the entire 500-meter section [E80].

Conceded: operating cash flow and free cash flow turned negative at Rs -2 Cr for March 2026 [E30, E31], producing a cash conversion of -0.07x [E29]. However, this cash burn occurs alongside aggressive top-line expansion, including compounded sales growth of 84% in the trailing twelve months and 70% over 5 years [E14, E16], which naturally demands working capital deployment for ongoing projects. While borrowings increased to Rs 24 Cr by September 2026 [E34], debt to equity remains low at a conservatively financed 0.14x alongside a comfortable current ratio of 2.09x [E32, E33]. Conceded: the dividend yield is 0.00% [E4], but the company is reinvesting capital into a robust portfolio of 25 premium residential projects [E71], driving high returns with an ROCE of 25.8% and ROE of 20.5% [E12, E13]. Furthermore, institutional investors are actively increasing their stake, with foreign holdings rising by 12.27 percentage points and total institutional money flow registering as positive [E37, E39]. Finally, while one project faces a government stay [E80], execution continues steadily across multiple other sites like Rashmi Square, which is nearing completion and slated for delivery in FY27 [E72, E84].

Conceded: sales growth reached 84% in the trailing twelve months and 70% over 5 years [E14, E16]. However, the bull's excuse for negative cash flow ignores the severity of a cash conversion of -0.07x and Rs -2 Cr in both operating and free cash flow for March 2026 [E29, E30, E31]. While debt-to-equity is cited as a safe 0.14x [E32], borrowings actually quadrupled from Rs 6 Cr to Rs 24 Cr by September 2026 [E34]. Conceded: the company boasts an ROCE of 25.8% and ROE of 20.5% [E12, E13], alongside rising institutional participation [E37, E39]. Yet, this performance fails to translate into shareholder payouts, as evidenced by a 0.00% dividend yield [E4] and ongoing promoter selling where holdings dropped by 7.24 percentage points [E36]. Finally, dismissing government hurdles ignores the explicit risk that the Rashmi Govind Dalvi project is currently on hold due to a government stay [E80].

Conceded: operating cash flow and free cash flow dropped to Rs -2 Cr with a cash conversion of -0.07x in March 2026 [E29, E30, E31], and borrowings increased to Rs 24 Cr by September 2026 [E34]. However, this short-term capital deployment supports aggressive business expansion, evidenced by compounded sales growth of 70% over 5 years and 84% in the trailing twelve months alongside a comfortable current ratio of 2.09x [E14, E16, E33]. Conceded: dividend yield is 0.00% and promoter holding decreased by 7.24 percentage points [E4, E36]. Yet, this capital retention fuels extraordinary underlying returns, demonstrated by an ROCE of 25.8% and an ROE of 20.5% that drastically outperform sector benchmarks [E10, E12, E13]. Furthermore, foreign institutions have heavily increased their stake by 12.27 percentage points, reflecting massive institutional confidence that overrides promoter reduction [E37]. Finally, while one project faces a government stay, the company maintains a robust portfolio of 25 premium residential projects with steady execution across multiple sites like Rashmi Square and Rashmi Delight [E71, E72, E80].

Conceded: sales compounded at 70% over 5 years and 84% in the trailing twelve months [E14, E16]. However, the bull frames negative cash flows of Rs -2 Cr and a cash conversion of -0.07x as mere capital deployment [E29, E30, E31], ignoring that rising borrowings from Rs 6 Cr to Rs 24 Cr in September 2026 expose the balance sheet as the top-line scales [E34]. Conceded: ROCE stands at 25.8% and ROE at 20.5% [E12, E13]. Yet, this stellar profitability fails to convert into actual cash returns for shareholders, as evidenced by a 0.00% dividend yield and ongoing insider selling that saw promoter holdings drop by 7.24 percentage points [E4, E36]. Conceded: the portfolio spans 25 projects with active execution cited at Rashmi Square and Rashmi Delight [E71, E72]. Nevertheless, this bullish diversification narrative glosses over concrete execution hazards, such as the government-imposed stay halting the Rashmi Govind Dalvi project entirely [E80]. Finally, while the bull leans on institutional inflows [E37], it downplays the valuation risk of trading at a P/E of 24.87x against a sector benchmark of 21.86x and a P/B of 5.12x against a sector benchmark of 1.35x [E6, E7].
